meta.title: MCP Question Bank — Chapter 16: Community, Governance & Security
meta.revision: v2.1 (curated 2026-09-12, 200 items, verified against the 2026-07-28 specification)

questions.question: Which role can veto any decision made by Core Maintainers or Maintainers?

options.text: Lead Maintainers, who must also publicly articulate their reasoning
The Linux Foundation board, through LF Projects LLC
Core Maintainers, by majority vote of the group
The Security Interest Group, for any decision that has security impact

questions.explanation: Lead Maintainers hold final authority, the BDFL role, can veto any decision, appoint and remove Core Maintainers, and are expected to publicly articulate their reasoning. Core Maintainers can veto Maintainer decisions by majority.

questions.question: How is membership in MCP's maintainer groups allocated?

options.text: To companies, which nominate a representative for each seat they hold
To individuals on merit, with no reserved company seats and no term limits
To individuals, but limited to two-year renewable terms
To individuals nominated by the Linux Foundation board

questions.explanation: Membership in the technical governance process is for individuals, not companies: there are no seats reserved for specific companies, membership follows the person rather than their employer, and it has no term limit.

questions.question: How does a proposed change to the specification move forward?

options.text: As an issue in the specification repository, closed once consensus appears
As a direct commit by a Core Maintainer, since they have admin access
As an RFC email to the maintainers' mailing list, voted on at the next meeting
As a SEP: a pull request with a sponsoring maintainer and status tracked by labels

questions.explanation: Specification Enhancement Proposals are the mechanism: markdown files in the seps/ directory, PR-derived numbering, a sponsoring maintainer and status managed through PR labels. Even Lead Maintainers use the same pull-request process as external contributors.

questions.question: A proposal needs a decision from the Steering Group. Which people is that?

options.text: Lead Maintainers and Core Maintainers only
One nominated representative from each contributing company
The Linux Foundation board members who oversee the AAIF
Lead Maintainers, Core Maintainers and Maintainers together

questions.explanation: The Steering Group is the top three tiers — Lead Maintainers, Core Maintainers and Maintainers — with Contributors outside it. Lead Maintainers additionally hold a BDFL veto, and no seat is held by a company.

questions.question: You find an authentication bypass in a reference implementation. What is the correct first move?

options.text: Post the details to the community discussion forum for triage
Open a private security advisory on the affected GitHub repository
Email the Linux Foundation, which coordinates disclosure for all AAIF projects
File a public issue so that maintainers and users see it at the same time

questions.explanation: Reporting goes through GitHub's private advisory mechanism on the affected repository, which keeps details embargoed while a fix is prepared. A public issue or forum post discloses the flaw to attackers along with everyone else.

questions.question: Under which licences are MCP's specifications and its non-specification documentation published?

options.text: Specifications and code under Apache 2.0; other documentation under CC BY 4.0
Everything under Apache 2.0, with contributors assigning copyright to the LF
Specifications under CC BY 4.0; code and documentation under Apache 2.0
Everything under CC BY 4.0, with code dual-licensed under MIT

questions.explanation: All code and specification contributions use Apache 2.0, while documentation excluding specifications uses CC BY 4.0. Contributors retain their copyright; no assignment is required.

questions.question: A reviewer asks why the specification says nothing about a local peer flooding a stdio server until it falls over. What is the answer?

options.text: It is covered indirectly, because authorization is mandatory for stdio servers
It is a transport concern, so the fix belongs in the SDK rather than the specification
Denial of service by a stdio peer is outside the threat model, since that peer already runs locally
It is covered by the rate limits that the specification requires every stdio server to implement itself

questions.explanation: A stdio peer is a local process launched by the host, already inside the trust boundary, so exhausting it is not a protocol-level threat. Authorization is explicitly not used on stdio, where credentials come from the environment.
